provenance.author: Paignia numerical-oracle lane, 2026-11-15
provenance.derivation: Original finite rational examples solved by dominance, indifference and payoff identities; no solver output copied.

assumptions.game: Two players; A[i][j] is row payoff and B[i][j] is column payoff; all cells present, finite rational values, independent mixed strategies p and q.
assumptions.witness: Each listed profile is checked, never generated by a Nash solver. Pure distributions and zero-probability strategies are allowed.
assumptions.residuals: g_row=max_i(Aq)_i-p^T A q; g_column=max_j(p^T B)_j-p^T B q. Both must be exactly zero for these exact witnesses.
assumptions.tolerance: 0 (exact rational arithmetic, no normalization or epsilon rounding). Not a production tolerance policy.
assumptions.catalogue: Coverage descriptions apply to mathematical examples only; no production result envelope, algorithm promise or completeness contract is defined.
assumptions.algorithms: Support enumeration and Lemke-Howson are not executed or implemented. This corpus cannot establish either algorithm's correctness or enumeration guarantees.

games.proof: Row 0 beats row 1 by 1 in either column; column 0 beats column 1 by 1 in either row. Both upstream indifference denominators are zero, so the inspected legacy helper would choose half/half; that candidate has gains 1/2 and 1/2. This is source algebra, not an executed upstream test.
Row values are 2q0-1 and 1-2q0; column values are 1-2p0 and 2p0-1. Indifference forces p0=q0=1/2; every pure outcome has a profitable deviation.

Two diagonal pure equilibria. If one player mixes both actions, the other must also mix because every payoff column/row has a strict best response. Indifference gives 2q0=1-q0 and p0=2(1-p0). These exhaust the pure/mixed support possibilities for this nondegenerate 2x2 example only.
Row indifference: 3q0=2-q0. Column indifference: 3-2p0=2p0. Each pure cell has a profitable deviation.
Column 2 is strictly dominated by either other column. The remaining game is matching pennies.
Player-swapped transpose of rectangular_2x3; row 2 is strictly dominated.
Every pure payoff is zero, so every independent mixed profile has zero deviation gain. A finite list is never an exhaustive listing of this continuum.
Neither player has an alternative action; negative utility is not an error or economic zero.
